Use `faker_qa/generator_parse_format_call_frequency_decoys/files/testcase.py`, class `TestGeneratorParseFormatCallFrequencyDecoysQA`, method `test_generator_parse_format_call_frequency_decoys_case`. The test seeds with `Faker.seed(314159)`, registers **four** argument groups via `set_arguments` (`rng_lo`, `rng_hi`, `orphan`, `decoy`), then calls `fake.parse(template)` where `template` contains eight `{{ ... }}` tokens mixing `pyint` with named groups and several color-related formatters (`hex_color`, `rgb_color`, `rgb_css_color`, `color_name`). Some registered groups are never referenced by any token (decoys). Under the runtime semantics of `faker/generator.py` (`parse` → `_re_token.sub` → `__format_token` → `format`), exactly how many **calls** are made to `faker.generator.format` (the traced name is `faker.generator.format`, i.e. `Generator.format`) during that single `parse` invocation?
